paper.title: Rational design of nanoscale stabilized oxide catalysts for OER with OC22
paper.research_summary: This work uses pre-trained OC22 machine learning models to interpolate total energy predictions for OER surface intermediates on 4119 oxide materials, then constructs a flexible high-throughput screening framework to identify viable anode catalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) under bulk and nanoscale Pourbaix stability, material cost, overpotential, and metastability constraints — identifying 122 bulk and 68 nanoscale candidates.

task.task_name_raw: Rational design of nanoscale stabilized oxide catalysts for OER
task.objective: Identify viable candidate anode catalysts for OER under varying reaction conditions for bulk, surface, and nanoscale Pourbaix stability as well as material cost, overpotential, and metastability.
input_requirements: slab structures up to Miller index 1
output_goal: 122 bulk-stable and 68 nanoscale-stable OER catalyst candidates

evidence.text: To demonstrate the full utility of this database, we constructed a flexible screening framework to identify viable candidate anode catalysts for OER under varying reaction conditions for bulk, surface, and nanoscale Pourbaix stability as well as material cost, overpotential, and metastability.
From our assessment, we were able to identify 122 and 68 viable candidates for OER under the bulk and nanoscale regime, respectively.

stages.stage_goal: Construct slab models for all facets up to maximum Miller index of 1 for oxide materials.
stage_output: slabs with atomic and vacuum layers ~12.5 Å thick
all terminations for each facet (excluding slabs >200 atoms)

evidence.text: We described all facets up to a MMI of 1 containning an atomic and vacuum layer of ca. 12.5 Å thick. The bulk materials used for slab construction in this study were obtained from the Materials Project.

stages.stage_goal: Adapt pre-trained GemNet-OC architecture for oxide surface and intermediate energy prediction.

evidence.text: We used a pre-trained model for the Structure to Energy and Forces (S2EF)-Total task from the OC22 framework to perform all machine learning predictions of the relaxed structure and total energy. The entirety of the Open Catalyst 2020 (OC20) dataset (1281040 DFT relaxations) was used to train an S2EF-Total model which was subsequently fine-tuned with the OC22 dataset (62331 DFT relaxations) to better predict the total energies of oxide surfaces and surface intermediates.

stages.stage_name_raw: Validation of ML predictions against DFT
stages.stage_goal: Assess accuracy of ML-predicted adsorption energies and overpotentials using DFT calculations.
stage_input: 85 Gibbs adsorption energy values from DFT

evidence.text: We used DFT to validate 85 values for Gibbs adsorption energy corresponding to eqn (6)–(8) for 33 Pourbaix stable compounds in our database. The MAE of the test set shown in Fig. 7(a) is 0.42 which is larger than the MAE of 0.239 eV obtained from the validation set in the original OC22 assessment.

stages.stage_name_raw: Interpolation of total energies for OER intermediates
stages.stage_goal: Predict total energies for all slabs and OER surface intermediates (O*, OH*, OOH*) for 4119 oxides.

evidence.text: In this work, we interpolated a database of the total energy predictions for all slabs and OER surface intermediates for 4119 oxide materials in the original OC22 dataset using pre-trained models from the OC22 framework.
Using the previously developed ML models, we systematically extrapolated the total DFT energy of all terminations for all facets up to a MMI = 1 for all 4119 materials considered in this study.

stages.stage_goal: Filter candidates using tiered criteria: (1) presence in OC22 training set, (2) bulk Pourbaix stability, (3) Wulff shape surface stability, (4) low overpotential, (5) energy above hull, (6) material cost; plus nanoscale extension.

evidence.text: In total we have identified 190 candidates (122 bulk – and 68 nanostable) with 145 distinct chemical systems when considering all the different screening frameworks listed in Table 2.

stages.stage_name_raw: Nanoscale stability assessment via nanoparticle formation energy
stages.stage_goal: Evaluate thermodynamic viability of metastable oxides as nanoparticles using GNP_f calculation.

evidence.text: To determine the nanoscale stability of metastable and unstable materials under operating conditions, we assessed the nanoparticle formation energy given by: GNP_f = EV(pH, V, T)(4/3 πr³) + γ̄(pH, V, T, ΔμM)(4πr²)
Using our nanoscale stability diagrams (see Fig. 2), we were able to identify 2778 Pourbaix stable materials with 886 stabilizing at the nanoscale regime (10 to 100 nm).
